src/content/model/statements/reassessmen.qualifiers: Following input triggers reassessment after delivery; when justified conditions subsequent input. Stopping and revision remain explicit.
src/content/model/statements/reassessmen.evidenceSeparation: Unresolved confidence and unvalidated observations remain explicit. Temporal change alone does not establish causation or classify uncertain outcomes as successes.
src/content/model/statements/reassessmen.alignment: ARG-003 presents the final practical conclusion with its actual two premises and canonical alternatives. Ending the reading path does not imply continued treatment.
src/content/model/statements/reassessmen.inferenceAndImpact: ARG-003 remains a defeasible iterative method. S-025 conceptual revision impact informs success interpretation but is not silently added as an argument premise. Reviewed complete participation: concluding arguments ARG-003; premise arguments none.

src/content/model/statements/regulatory-.proposition: empirical: Neural regulation operates with incomplete information and within biological constraints and competing demands. Canonical text and metadata are unchanged from reviewed Stage 4.
src/content/model/statements/regulatory-.qualifiers: Incomplete information, biological constraints, and competing demands name distinct limits, without asserting every response is poor or improvable.
src/content/model/statements/regulatory-.evidenceSeparation: Combined appraisal remains unresolved. Examples associated with S-018/S-008 do not establish every limitation or their interactions.
src/content/model/statements/regulatory-.alignment: The section framing and full explanation preserve estimation, feasibility, and tradeoff distinctions. No new premise is inferred by its placement before S-008.
src/content/model/statements/regulatory-.inferenceAndImpact: ARG-005 premise 4 remains defeasible. A locally best feasible response can coexist with these limits; no dependency or claimed route to beneficial modifiability was added. Reviewed complete participation: concluding arguments none; premise arguments ARG-005.

src/content/model/statements/salient-per.proposition: empirical: A sufficiently salient neurobiomechanical perturbation can prompt reevaluation and reorganization of an established neuromotor strategy. Canonical text and metadata are unchanged from reviewed Stage 4.
src/content/model/statements/salient-per.qualifiers: Sufficiently salient defines a condition to specify independently of success; can asserts capacity, not inevitable reorganization or improvement.
src/content/model/statements/salient-per.evidenceSeparation: Unresolved confidence and no documented claim-specific appraisal remain visible. A general perturbation hypothesis supplies no chiropractic occurrence evidence.
src/content/model/statements/salient-per.alignment: The actual-input-effects section retains this general-mechanism boundary in its explanation, followed by separate S-011 and S-028 claims. No adjacency-based argument is displayed.
src/content/model/statements/salient-per.inferenceAndImpact: S-008 conceptual impact and S-020 see-also remain revision/reference information. S-028 carries the specific mechanism claim; there are no recorded arguments using or concluding S-010. Reviewed complete participation: concluding arguments none; premise arguments none.

src/content/model/statements/sensory-upd.proposition: empirical: The nervous system updates its estimates using incoming sensory information, and new sensory information can lead to reorganization of neuromotor strategies. Canonical text and metadata are unchanged from reviewed Stage 4.
src/content/model/statements/sensory-upd.qualifiers: Can lead asserts sensory contribution capacity; updating estimates and changing strategies are distinct, with no guarantee of benefit.
src/content/model/statements/sensory-upd.evidenceSeparation: The Shadmehr/Mussa-Ivaldi source and its practice/mechanical confounds remain visible. Confidence stays unresolved; no chiropractic effect follows from the example.
src/content/model/statements/sensory-upd.alignment: Living-organisms ends with the full joint empirical claim, preserving updating versus strategy change and its complete limits and revision tests.
src/content/model/statements/sensory-upd.inferenceAndImpact: ARG-005 receives premise 6. S-018/S-008 conceptual dependencies and S-010 see-also do not become argument edges or proof of the specific perturbation mechanism. Reviewed complete participation: concluding arguments none; premise arguments ARG-005.

src/content/model/statements/state-depen.proposition: empirical: Neuromotor function varies with the person's state, task, and environment; in some circumstances, the available motor strategies are limited or poorly suited to current demands. Canonical text and metadata are unchanged from reviewed Stage 4.
src/content/model/statements/state-depen.qualifiers: In some circumstances limits the poor-fit claim. Context dependence alone does not assert universal limitation or a modifiable opportunity.
src/content/model/statements/state-depen.evidenceSeparation: Carpenter and Gribble examples remain task-bounded, with their limiting notes intact. Unresolved confidence does not weaken the asserted context dependence.
src/content/model/statements/state-depen.alignment: Living-organisms introduces the exact motor-control proposition. Full explanations retain tissue, task, and measurement alternatives and reject a universal symmetry or tone criterion.
src/content/model/statements/state-depen.inferenceAndImpact: Premise 5 of ARG-005 remains distinct from conceptual revision effects on S-009/S-010/S-020/S-023. All those effects remain visible without being projected as arguments. Reviewed complete participation: concluding arguments none; premise arguments ARG-005.

src/content/model/statements/success-and.proposition: value: Every successful adjustment provides a functional benefit within its specified neuromotor scope, context, and timescale. Canonical text and metadata are unchanged from reviewed Stage 4.
src/content/model/statements/success-and.qualifiers: Every ranges over defined successful adjustments, not all delivered inputs or every reorganization. Specified scope and timescale are preserved.
src/content/model/statements/success-and.evidenceSeparation: Value classification and not-applicable confidence are separate from the deductive label. The conclusion remains compatible with zero successful adjustments.
src/content/model/statements/success-and.alignment: ARG-006 presents the conclusion together with all three premises and the full canonical inference, with no duplicate standalone conclusion step.
src/content/model/statements/success-and.inferenceAndImpact: The deduction applies S-022 to the improving change defined by S-024/S-025 in the same scope. S-026 is not substituted into ARG-007 or any occurrence claim. Reviewed complete participation: concluding arguments ARG-006; premise arguments none.

src/content/model/statements/successful-.proposition: definition: A successful adjustment is an adjustment that improves context-appropriate human function within a specified neuromotor scope, context, and timescale. Canonical text and metadata are unchanged from reviewed Stage 4.
src/content/model/statements/successful-.qualifiers: Success requires qualifying improvement in a specified neuromotor comparison; uncertain observations do not settle its fulfillment.
src/content/model/statements/successful-.evidenceSeparation: Definition and not-applicable confidence do not assert that any success occurs. Occurrence belongs to independent empirical S-011.
src/content/model/statements/successful-.alignment: The full definition and its all-input accounting remain accessible; neither the section question nor the metadata presents success as an observed result.
src/content/model/statements/successful-.inferenceAndImpact: ARG-006 uses this premise to evaluate qualifying successes. It is absent from ARG-007, which uses S-011. S-024/S-021 conceptual roles and S-016 revision effects do not add argument premises. Reviewed complete participation: concluding arguments none; premise arguments ARG-006.
